ev.sibling_ill.text.1: Your little brother or sister is burning with fever. The adults whisper anxiously.
ev.sibling_ill.text.2: The youngest in the house has been burning with fever for three days and won't eat. The healer shook her head and said the next few nights will decide it.
ev.sibling_ill.text.3: The little one coughs so hard you can hear it through the wall, and the forehead is as hot as a hearthstone. The grown-ups take turns at the bedside and try not to meet each other's eyes.
ev.sibling_ill.text.4: A rash with fever has been going round the little ones in the neighborhood, and now it has come to your house. Your little brother or sister lies covered in red spots, burning hot, calling your name.
ev.sibling_ill.text.5: On a hot day the little one drank from the puddle by the well while nobody was looking. Now there is fever and sickness, and the child is wasting away before your eyes.
ev.sibling_ill.text.6: The house is strangely quiet: nobody stomping about, nobody fighting over the spoon. The youngest lies in the corner, hot and limp, not even asking for a story.
ev.sibling_ill.text.7: The little one got soaked through in a cold rain and was coughing by nightfall. By morning the fever is so high that a wet cloth on the forehead dries in no time.
ev.sibling_ill.text.8: In the night you woke because the little one beside you was hot as a coal and mumbling nonsense. The grown-ups stirred up the fire and didn't lie down again till morning.
ev.sibling_ill.text.9: The healer left a bitter brew and said the little one must drink it every hour, day and night. The grown-ups have to work, so the pot of brew was pushed into your hands.
ev.sibling_ill.text.10: A fever has been going from yard to yard, and yesterday it looked in on you. The youngest lies flat, burning up, and recognizes no one but you.
ev.sibling_ill.text.11: The little one is so weak from fever that the head won't stay up. The grown-ups whisper by the door, and from their voices you understand more than they say.
ev.sibling_ill.text.12: The little one scraped a knee on a stone, and three days later the leg swelled up and the fever began. The healer washed the wound and said: now we can only wait.
ev.sibling_ill.text.13: The sickly season has come: mist in the mornings, mosquitoes in the evenings. The youngest shakes with chills, though the forehead is blazing.
ev.sibling_ill.text.14: The grown-ups went off for the whole day and left you in charge, and by noon the little one is burning up and crying without a voice.
ev.sibling_ill.text.15: All night someone has to change the wet cloth on the little one's forehead and give sips from a spoon. The grown-ups are dropping with exhaustion, and the fever still won't go.
ev.sibling_ill.text.16: Only yesterday you and the little one were chasing each other round the yard, and today there's a fever, cloudy eyes, and not even the favorite toy is wanted.
ev.found_coin.text.1: You found a coin in the street. Nobody saw.
ev.found_coin.text.1.MAY: By the road you found a dropped pouch of cacao beans. No one saw.
ev.found_coin.text.2: As the traders were packing up their stalls, you spotted a shiny coin under a counter. The owner had already gone, and no one was around.
ev.found_coin.text.3: Something glinted among the pebbles at the bottom of the stream. You waded into the cold water and fished out a coin - old and green, but real.
ev.found_coin.title.3: At the Bottom of the Stream
ev.found_coin.text.4: The morning after the festival the square is littered with shells and scraps of ribbon. And in a crack between the stones lies a coin someone dropped in the crush.
ev.found_coin.text.5: You were prising a pebble out of an old wall, and a coin fell out with it. Someone hid it there long ago - and evidently forgot.
ev.found_coin.title.5: A Hiding Place in the Wall
ev.found_coin.text.6: Travelers were crowding at the town gate, and in the bustle someone dropped a coin. It rolled right up to your feet - and nobody turned round.
ev.found_coin.text.7: Raking the ashes out of the old hearth in the yard, you felt something hard - a coin, black with soot. No one saw.
ev.found_coin.text.8: On the way home you kicked a pebble, and under it was a coin, half pressed into the mud.
ev.found_coin.text.9: The downpour washed out the path by the market, and the edge of a coin peeped out of the mud. You looked around - nobody.
ev.found_coin.text.10: A richly dressed man walked past, and something fell out of his purse. By the time you'd picked up the coin, he was long gone.
ev.found_coin.text.11: By the well, in the wet grass, you found a coin. One of the people who came for water must have dropped it - but who, there's no telling now.
ev.found_coin.text.12: You climbed a tree after a bird's nest, and instead of eggs there was a shiny coin. Some bird must have carried it there.
ev.found_coin.text.13: You and the other children were digging a hole on the riverbank, and your stick clinked against a coin. The others had just run off to the water and noticed nothing.
ev.found_coin.text.14: Helping sweep out a shop for a couple of sweets, you found a coin under the doorstep. The owner is dozing in the corner and saw nothing.
ev.found_coin.text.15: In a crowd gawking at wandering performers, someone's purse jingled and a coin dropped at your feet. By the time you bent down, the crowd had already moved on.
ev.found_coin.text.16: A coin was stuck between the planks of an old footbridge. You spent ages fishing for it with a twig and finally got it out. No one saw.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text.1: The jar of oil lies in pieces. Father asks who did it, and {npc} silently looks at you. You both knocked it over, fighting for the last sweet cake.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text.1.E03: The amphora of oil lies in pieces. Father asks who did it, and {npc} silently looks at you. You both knocked it over, fighting for the last fig.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text.2: The shelf of crockery has come down off the wall, shards all over the floor. Father stands in the doorway waiting for an answer, and {npc} is studying their own feet. You both set it swinging, arguing over who could reach higher.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text.3: The stew you were told to watch has burnt onto the pot past scraping. Father sniffs and asks who's to blame. {npc} stares at the floor - though you both ran off to play.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text.4: The net Father spent three evenings mending is full of holes again: you were playing tug-of-war with it, pretending to be fishermen. Father asks whose work this is, and {npc} silently looks at you.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text.5: The flatbreads saved for tomorrow have vanished from the shelf. Father frowns; {npc} puts on an innocent face. You both ate them - taking turns while no one was looking.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text.6: Father's knife turned up by the stream with its tip snapped off: you took it to carve little boats and fought over who went first. Father asks who took it, and {npc} says nothing.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text.7: You were left to mind the fire, but you argued over whose turn it was to feed it, and it went out. Father came home to a cold house and asks who's to blame. {npc} silently looks at you.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text.8: The festival shirt is torn along the seam - you each pulled it your way, deciding whose turn it was to wear it. Father holds it up and asks who did this. {npc} looks away.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text.9: The sack of grain is torn and grain is scattered all over the yard. Father asks who did it, and {npc} looks at you and says nothing. You tore it together, playing robbers.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text.10: A branch of the neighbor's fruit tree is broken, and the neighbor has already been round to complain. Father asks who climbed it, and {npc} is very carefully looking elsewhere. You both did - racing each other.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text.11: The beds behind the house are trampled: you chased each other right across the seedlings. Father stands over them and asks who did it. {npc} says nothing, but gives you a very meaningful look.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text.12: The door has been knocked off its place: you both threw yourselves at it - one holding, one pushing. Father asks who's responsible, and {npc} has suddenly become very interested in the ceiling.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text.13: The bucket has fallen down the well: you argued over who would pull the rope, and let go of it. Father asks who's to blame, and {npc} silently looks at you.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text.14: Half the sweets set aside for guests have been eaten. Father counts what's left and asks who did it. {npc} looks at you, licking sticky fingers - though you both kept sneaking them.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text.15: The new blanket is scorched and black with soot - you were wrestling by the hearth and knocked the embers onto it. Father asks who's to blame, and {npc} silently looks at you.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text.16: The water you'd been hauling all morning went everywhere in one go: you were shoving at the tub over who'd drink first. Father looks at the wet floor and asks who's to blame. {npc} says nothing.
ev.c_first_steps.text.1: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} took {g=npc_sex:his|her} first steps: three steps from the hearth straight to you - then sat down hard, looking as if that had been the plan all along. The whole household clapped as if at a festival.
ev.c_first_steps.text.1.E03: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} took {g=npc_sex:his|her} first steps: three steps from the hearth straight to you - then sat down hard, looking as if that had been the plan all along. The whole household clapped as if at the games.
ev.c_first_steps.text.2: {npc} took {g=npc_sex:his|her} first steps holding on to the tail of a very patient dog. The dog pretended not to notice.
ev.c_first_steps.text.3: {npc} let go of the bench and set off walking - straight for the bowl of food. Clearly the destination had been chosen in advance.
ev.c_first_steps.text.4: You turned away for just a moment, and {npc} was already standing in the middle of the yard with nothing to hold, swaying and beaming with pride. You missed the first steps, but the whole neighborhood saw the second ones.
ev.c_first_steps.text.5: While everyone sat at the festive meal, {npc} got up and toddled across the whole room to the guests. The guests decided it was a good omen.
ev.c_first_steps.text.6: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} is walking! So far only from wall to wall and back, but with a face as serious as a messenger bearing important news.
ev.c_first_steps.text.7: In the morning {npc} stood up on wobbly legs, and by evening was running away from you across the yard, squealing with delight. Peace and quiet in this house are over.
ev.c_first_steps.text.8: {npc} took {g=npc_sex:his|her} first steps in the rain - stepped out from under the eaves straight into a puddle and burst out laughing. Everything had to be dried, but you smiled all day.
ev.c_first_steps.text.9: For a whole week the neighbors' children led the little one around by the hands, and at last {npc} walked alone. The children are strutting about as if it were all their doing.
ev.c_first_steps.text.10: {npc} took a step, plopped down, got up, stepped again - twenty times in a row, until falling asleep right there on the floor. That stubbornness clearly comes from you.
ev.c_first_steps.text.11: You were working in the yard when you felt someone clutching your clothes. It was {npc} - {g=npc_sex:he'd|she'd} walked all the way from the doorstep, for the first time without a hand to hold.
ev.c_first_steps.text.12: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} started walking - and the very first thing {g=npc_sex:he|she} did was knock over the water pot. You mopped the floor and laughed: nothing in this house will stay on a low shelf now.
ev.c_first_steps.text.13: At the market {npc} wriggled out of your arms and took three steps toward the woman selling sweets. She was so touched that she handed over a treat for free.
ev.c_first_steps.text.14: {npc} took {g=npc_sex:his|her} first steps at dawn while the whole house slept, and you were the only witness. You decided not to tell anyone until tomorrow: let this morning belong to just the two of you.
ev.c_first_steps.text.15: Everyone in the house sat in a circle and called the little one by name. {npc} stood, thought about it, and set off walking - to you, of course.
ev.c_first_steps.text.16: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} learned to walk and immediately learned to run off. Now someone in the house is always shouting, "Where's {npc}?!"
ev.c_teething.text.1: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} screams night after night: the teeth are coming. The neighbor says rub the gums with honey, Grandmother says hang a wolf's tooth round the neck. You've tried both and are ready to bite someone yourself.
ev.c_teething.text.2: {npc} gnaws on everything within reach: spoons, the edge of the table, your finger. The teeth are coming through - and your patience seems to be wearing through with them.
ev.c_teething.text.3: For the third night running {npc} has cried until dawn: a tooth is coming. You've paced the house with the baby in your arms so much it should count as a long journey.
ev.c_teething.text.4: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} has been fussing all day: red cheeks, drool everywhere. The neighbor looked in, felt the gums and gave her verdict: teeth.
ev.c_teething.text.5: The healer gave you a little root and said to let the baby chew it. {npc} chews it with great pleasure - and still screams at night.
ev.c_teething.text.6: {npc} won't sleep and won't let anyone else sleep either. The neighbors through the wall already know you're teething and nod sympathetically in the mornings.
ev.c_teething.text.7: At last the first tooth appeared - tiny, white and sharp. You found out when {npc} bit your finger.
ev.c_teething.text.8: Teeth. {npc} whimpers, then runs hot, then suddenly laughs as if nothing were wrong. You're so tired you fall asleep sitting up.
ev.c_teething.text.9: One person recommends cold water, another a dry crust, another a charm. {npc} calmly rejects them all and keeps on screaming.
ev.c_teething.text.10: In the night you leapt up at the crying for the fifth time. The baby is teething, and you seem to be losing what's left of your mind.
ev.c_teething.text.11: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} refuses food, stuffs a fist in {g=npc_sex:his|her} mouth and gives you a reproachful look, as if every tooth were your fault.
ev.c_teething.text.12: All night you rocked the cradle while {npc} kept whimpering: teeth again. Towards morning you both fell asleep - you right on the floor beside the cradle.
ev.c_teething.text.13: {npc} has chewed the edge of your best shawl to rags: teething. You're sorry for the shawl, but sorrier still for yourself after another sleepless night.
ev.c_teething.text.14: A neighbor shared a sure remedy: rub the gums with something bitter. {npc} screwed up {g=npc_sex:his|her} face, took offense at the whole world and screamed even louder.
ev.c_teething.text.15: The second tooth, the third… {npc} hasn't smiled in ages and whimpers all the time. You started counting the days till this ordeal ends and lost count.
ev.c_teething.text.16: By day {npc} is meekness itself; by night, a small thunderstorm: teeth. Everyone in the house has red eyes.
ev.a_mother_visit.text.1: {npc}, your mother, came with a basket of flatbreads and a year's worth of advice. The flatbreads were gone that evening; the advice will stay with you longer.
ev.a_mother_visit.text.2: {npc}, your mother, dropped in "for a moment" and stayed till evening. She rearranged all your pots, praised your stew, and remarked that it was a little salty.
ev.a_mother_visit.text.3: {npc}, your mother, brought a bundle of dried berries and half a year's worth of news about every neighbor. You'd asked for neither, but both came in handy.
ev.a_mother_visit.text.4: {npc}, your mother, sat by your hearth telling stories about what you were like as a child. Half of them you don't remember, and the other half you'd rather forget.
ev.a_mother_visit.text.5: {npc}, your mother, came a long way to see you. The road was dusty, but her tongue was as sharp as ever: everyone who came into the house got a piece of advice.
ev.a_mother_visit.text.6: {npc}, your mother, brought a warm wrap she'd been sewing in the evenings. It came out a bit lopsided, but you wear it with pride.
ev.a_mother_visit.text.7: {npc}, your mother, came in and set to work without a word: swept, mended, scrubbed. You meant to object, but suddenly felt small again - and it was surprisingly pleasant.
ev.a_mother_visit.text.8: {npc}, your mother, arrived and asked from the doorstep whether you were eating properly. "Yes" didn't satisfy her: you had to eat in front of her.
ev.a_mother_visit.text.9: {npc}, your mother, stayed with you for three days. In that time you heard five old stories, three recipes and one opinion about your life - a very detailed one.
ev.a_mother_visit.text.10: {npc}, your mother, came for the festival with a basket full of food, as if your house were starving. The food lasted a week; the warmth lasted much longer.
ev.a_mother_visit.text.11: {npc}, your mother, brought healing herbs "just in case" and explained in detail what each one was for. You remembered none of it, but hung the herbs carefully by the hearth.
ev.a_mother_visit.text.12: {npc}, your mother, stayed late. You talked about everything and nothing, and suddenly you noticed how much grey there was in her hair.
ev.a_mother_visit.text.13: {npc}, your mother, spotted at once the hole in your clothes, the dust in the corner and the shadows under your eyes. She sewed up the hole, swept out the dust, and as for the shadows said: "Sleep more."
ev.a_mother_visit.text.14: {npc}, your mother, brought news from home: who'd been born, who'd died, who'd quarreled with whom. You listened and thought about how long it had been since you were there.
ev.a_mother_visit.text.15: {npc}, your mother, came to ask a small favor and while she was at it stayed for dinner, stayed the night and told off the neighbor's dog. When she left, the house was strangely quiet.
ev.a_mother_visit.text.16: {npc}, your mother, taught you an old recipe you'd never known. She says that's how it was made when she was a girl - and the food tasted of childhood.
ev.y_hungry_winter.text.1: It was a hungry winter. Mother divided each flatbread so that nothing was left for herself, and you learned to fall asleep without thinking about food.
ev.y_hungry_winter.text.2: The harvest failed, and the next one was a long way off. Mother made soup from herbs and roots, and you learned not to ask for more.
ev.y_hungry_winter.text.3: Before the new harvest there was nothing left in the house but bran. Mother mixed grass and pounded bark into the flatbreads, and you ate without wincing - there was no choice.
ev.y_hungry_winter.text.4: Drought ate the harvest. Every evening Mother divided the food into tiny heaps and slipped her own share to you - smiling as if she weren't hungry at all.
ev.y_hungry_winter.text.5: For a whole month there was so little food that you fell asleep hugging an empty belly. Mother told stories about feasts, and that made it both better and worse.
ev.y_hungry_winter.text.6: In the hungry season Mother went round the countryside gathering roots and wild fruit and took you along. You learned to tell what can be eaten and what is better left alone.
ev.y_hungry_winter.text.7: The rains flooded the fields and the grain rotted. All that season Mother cooked the same thin porridge and said that being full is only a habit.
ev.y_hungry_winter.text.8: You remember that hungry year by the way Mother avoided your eyes as she set your bowl down: there was even less in her own.
ev.y_hungry_winter.text.9: There was only enough food for one meal a day. Mother sent you to bed early: when you're asleep, you don't feel hungry.
ev.y_hungry_winter.text.10: In the hungry season Mother traded her only bracelet for a sack of grain. You saw her stroke her bare wrist when she thought no one was looking.
ev.y_hungry_winter.text.11: Grain got so dear that Mother came back from the market empty-handed. You learned to treasure every crumb and keep it in your mouth for a long time.
ev.y_hungry_winter.text.12: You remember that winter as cold and quiet: nobody laughed, everyone saved their strength. Mother got up first to blow the fire back to life and was the last to sit down to eat.
ev.y_hungry_winter.text.13: Hail flattened the fields in a single night. Until the next harvest Mother stretched the last of the flour as far as it would go, and you gleaned ears of grain with her in other people's fields.
ev.y_hungry_winter.text.14: There was nothing to eat at home, so you learned to catch tiny fish in the ditch. Mother cooked your catch and praised you as if you'd brought home a whole ox.
ev.y_hungry_winter.text.15: Empty pots, empty shelves, empty talk of food. Mother gave you her share and said she'd already eaten at the neighbor's - you knew it wasn't true.
ev.y_hungry_winter.text.16: Hunger came quietly: first two meals a day, then one. Mother never once complained; she just pulled the belt tighter - hers and yours.
ev.f_doubt.text.1: You prayed and brought offerings, and still misfortune came - not to the wicked, but to the best people you know. For the first time a thought rang out: is anyone listening?
ev.f_doubt.text.2: Your neighbor, the most honest man for miles, kept every rite all his life - and lost everything in one night's fire. Meanwhile the man who cheated everyone lives on and grows rich. Where is the justice in that?
ev.f_doubt.text.3: Pestilence swept through the district and took the righteous and the wicked alike. You stood by the fresh graves and couldn't understand what you had been praying for all year.
ev.f_doubt.text.4: You got talking to a traveler who believes something entirely different - and couldn't answer him. He is as sure he is right as you are. How can anyone know which of you is?
ev.f_doubt.text.5: You prayed for rain along with everyone else, and no rain fell all summer. People still go to prayers, but in many eyes you see the same question that torments you.
ev.f_doubt.text.6: You saw with your own eyes a respected servant of the faith take payment for what he ought to do for free, and lie to people's faces. If he behaves like that - what does he himself believe?
ev.f_doubt.text.7: Your friend has died - kind, generous, someone who never harmed a soul. Over the body they spoke of a higher plan, and you listened and could find no sense in it at all.
ev.f_doubt.text.8: A visiting sage in the square said that thunder, sickness and harvests follow their own laws, not the will of heaven. The crowd laughed, but you walked away deep in thought.
ev.f_doubt.text.9: You made a vow and kept it to the last detail, yet your plea went unanswered. At night you lie awake and ask the darkness: was there anyone there to listen?
ev.f_doubt.text.10: The neighbors' child has died - their only one, long awaited. All their lives they prayed harder than you. Watching their grief, for the first time you don't know what words to pray with yourself.
ev.f_doubt.text.11: An army passed through the district, and before the battle both sides prayed for the same victory. You looked at the burnt-out homes and wondered: which of them did heaven listen to - and did it listen at all?
ev.f_doubt.text.12: The miracle the whole district talked about turned out to be a clever trick - you saw for yourself how it was done. What if the other miracles are the same?
ev.f_doubt.text.13: No misfortune struck - it was just that one day, at prayer, you caught yourself repeating the words and feeling nothing. That emptiness frightened you more than any misfortune.
ev.f_doubt.text.14: Three years running, one blow after another: a failed harvest, sickness, debt. You kept every rite faithfully, and things only got worse. How did you anger heaven - or does heaven simply not care?
ev.f_doubt.text.15: Two learned servants of the faith argued in front of you about what pleases heaven, and fell out completely. If even they don't know the truth, how is an ordinary person to find it?
ev.f_doubt.text.16: Before your eyes an innocent man was punished, while the real culprit bought his way out and went off to thank heaven for his luck. You watched him go and didn't know whom to pray to any more.
ev.a_foundling.text.1: At dawn someone left a baby in a basket at the gate of a holy place. This is how the poor give up children they cannot feed: whoever picks the child up will raise it.
ev.a_foundling.text.1.E03: At dawn someone left a baby in a basket at the temple gate. This is how the poor give up children they cannot feed: whoever picks the child up will raise it.
ev.a_foundling.text.2: Early in the morning you heard faint crying by the well. In a basket covered with rags lay a baby - hungry, but alive. No one saw who left it.
ev.a_foundling.text.3: A woven basket had caught in the reeds by the bank, and in it lay a baby wrapped in old cloth. Someone must have set it on the current, hoping for a kind soul.
ev.a_foundling.text.4: In the morning you opened the door and nearly stepped on a basket. A baby was asleep inside, and beside it lay a little bundle with a handful of grain - all they could give.
ev.a_foundling.text.5: After a noisy market day a basket has been left under an empty stall. The traders have gone home, and a thin cry is coming from the basket.
ev.a_foundling.text.6: At the roadside, in the shade of a tree, stands a basket with a baby in it, shaded from the sun with leaves. Whoever left it at least took care of that.
ev.a_foundling.text.7: Another basket with a baby at the gate of the holy place. A sign has been stitched on the swaddling cloth: perhaps the woman who left it still hopes to find her child one day.
ev.a_foundling.text.8: In the night someone knocked softly at your door. When you opened it, the street was empty, and a basket with a baby stood on the step.
ev.a_foundling.text.9: On the steps of a wealthy house where you've come on business stands a basket with a baby in it. The servants pretend not to notice; the masters don't come out.
ev.a_foundling.text.10: In the basket by the gate is a girl, tiny as can be. They say girls are left more often: they eat just as much, and supposedly they're less use in the fields.
ev.a_foundling.text.11: It has been a hungry year, and there are more foundlings at the holy place. This morning you saw another basket - and the baby in it looked straight at you.
ev.a_foundling.text.12: A baby lies in a basket under the market awning, with a string of cheap beads round its neck - probably all someone had. Its crying is barely audible now.
ev.a_foundling.text.13: Walking along the path by a field, you heard crying in the tall grass. A basket with a baby had been set there so the first passer-by would see it.
ev.a_foundling.text.14: The morning after the festival a basket with a baby was found at the gate of the holy place. The keepers say they can't raise it without help from ordinary folk - and they are looking at you.
ev.a_foundling.text.15: Under the old tree where people leave offerings, someone has left a basket with a baby. They must have hoped good people wouldn't let it perish.
ev.a_foundling.text.16: At the inn where you stopped on your journey, a basket with a baby was found in the shed this morning. The innkeeper is cursing and threatening to carry it off to the gate of the holy place.
ev.c_lost.text.1: At the festival your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} got lost in the crowd. You spent half the day rushing round the market - and found the runaway in the square, front row, mouth open, listening to a storyteller.
ev.c_lost.text.1.E03: At the festival your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} got lost in the crowd. You spent half the day rushing round the market - and found the runaway by the temple, front row, mouth open, listening to a storyteller.
ev.c_lost.text.2: At the market {npc} let go of your hand - and a moment later was gone. The runaway turned up at a sweet stall, where the seller was already treating the "poor little orphan."
ev.c_lost.text.3: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} vanished in broad daylight. You ran round every yard in the neighborhood, while {npc} was asleep the whole time in a heap of straw behind the shed.
ev.c_lost.text.4: In the evening {npc} didn't come home. You searched the whole neighborhood with a torch half the night, and towards dawn {npc} walked in, filthy and happy: "We were catching frogs!"
ev.c_lost.text.5: In the festival crowd {npc} tagged along after some wandering musicians and ended up at the other end of town. You only found the runaway by evening - beating time and with no intention of coming home.
ev.c_lost.text.6: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} got lost gathering firewood at the edge of the woods. You shouted yourself hoarse, and it was an old herdsman who found {g=npc_sex:him|her}: {npc} was sitting on a stump telling the herd a story.
ev.c_lost.text.7: While you were haggling with the potter, {npc} disappeared. An hour later a strange woman brought {g=npc_sex:him|her} back: {npc} had told her your name and your street - exactly as you'd taught.
ev.c_lost.text.8: At the great festival by the holy place {npc} went missing. You went round the whole square three times, and the runaway turned up on the steps, helping some old man hand out flatbreads.
ev.c_lost.text.9: {npc} decided to find the way home from the market alone - and headed off in the opposite direction. The runaway was found by the town wall, already being fed sweets.
ev.c_lost.text.10: You roused the whole street: {npc} was missing! And all the while {g=npc_sex:he|she} was sitting up the tree behind the house, watching the search with great interest.
ev.c_lost.text.11: On the way to the next village {npc} fell behind, staring at something in a ditch. You ran back and found the straggler right there - a beetle in cupped hands and perfect calm on {g=npc_sex:his|her} face.
ev.c_lost.text.12: At dusk {npc} followed a stray dog and got lost in the back lanes. It was the same dog that led {g=npc_sex:him|her} home - and got the best bone in the house for it.
ev.c_lost.text.13: At the neighbors' wedding {npc} went missing. The whole party searched, and {npc} was asleep under the table, curled up among the guests' feet.
ev.c_lost.text.14: {npc} vanished from the house first thing in the morning. By noon you didn't know what to think, and by evening {npc} came back with the neighbors' children, who had "just gone to look at the big river."
ev.c_lost.text.15: In the crush at the town gate you let go of the little hand for a moment - and {npc} was gone. The runaway turned up at the well, washing and chatting busily with the water carrier.
ev.c_lost.text.16: For half the day {npc} was nowhere to be found, while you dashed between home and the market. It turned out {g=npc_sex:he'd|she'd} been at the old weaver's the whole time, learning to plait braid - "to make you a present."
ev.f_fasting.text.1: The fast has fallen in the hardest season of work. By midday your hands are shaking, and half the day is still ahead. You could ease off a little - who would see?
ev.f_fasting.text.1.islamic: Ramadan has fallen in the hot months. Not a sip of water from dawn to dusk, and the work won't wait: by midday circles swim before your eyes.
ev.f_fasting.text.1.jain: You took a long fast upon yourself - only boiled water, and only until sunset. On the fifth day your body begs for mercy.
ev.f_fasting.text.2: The neighbors are having a feast, and the smell of roasting meat drifts across the whole yard. You are keeping the fast, and your stomach growls so loudly it must be heard in the street.
ev.f_fasting.text.3: The fast caught you on the road. Your feet ache, the sun beats down, and the roadside inn smells so good… They say travelers are allowed some leniency - but you're not sure.
ev.f_fasting.text.4: On the third day of the fast your head started spinning right in the middle of work. A workmate pressed a flatbread into your hand: "Eat it, no one will know."
ev.f_fasting.text.5: An old friend has come from far away, and the table is laid as it hasn't been in ages. Everyone is eating, but you are fasting, and every mouthful the guests take feels like a reproach.
ev.f_fasting.text.6: You haven't yet recovered from an illness, and the fast has already begun. The healer says your body needs food; your conscience says a vow is a vow.
ev.f_fasting.text.7: The hottest time of year - and the hardest work. Sweat stings your eyes, your lips are cracked, and the end of the fast is still far off.
ev.f_fasting.text.8: At night you can't sleep for hunger. The leftovers of a feast are sitting in the storeroom, and a quiet voice inside whispers that one little bite won't matter.
ev.f_fasting.text.9: Your workmates tease you: "You're as pale as a wall - who needs your suffering?" They eat right in front of you and hold out their share.
ev.f_fasting.text.10: The fast has gone on a long time and your strength is giving out: you dropped a heavy load and barely jumped clear. And the work won't do itself.
ev.f_fasting.title.10: At the End of Your Strength
ev.f_fasting.text.11: You had to spend the whole day at the market among stalls of hot food. The woman opposite is frying flatbreads and seems to be fanning the smoke your way on purpose.
ev.f_fasting.text.12: This year you resolved to keep the fast more strictly than ever. But your body protests: your hands shake, your thoughts tangle, and even familiar work comes hard.
ev.f_fasting.text.13: A baker you know, unaware of your fast, pushed a warm flatbread into your hands straight from the fire: "Try it, never made a better one!" Refuse and you offend him; take it and you break your vow.
ev.f_fasting.text.14: The fast drags on endlessly, and the work doesn't let up. At night you dream of food, and by day you catch yourself counting the hours until evening.
ev.f_fasting.text.15: Working beside you are people of another faith, and your fast means nothing to them. They kindly offer to share their meal and can't understand why you torment yourself.
ev.f_fasting.text.16: Only one day of the fast is left, and you have no strength left at all. Surely no one would blame you for eating a little early - the feast is almost here anyway.
ev.v_rel_father_old.text.1: {npc} has aged and weakened: his hands shake, his eyes are cloudy, and he talks more and more about the past. Yesterday he called for you and said he wants to ask your forgiveness - for those nights.
ev.v_rel_father_old.text.2: {npc} has grown very weak and hardly gets up. Today he asked you to sit beside him, was silent for a long time, then said: "I know what I was. Can you forgive me?"
ev.v_rel_father_old.text.3: {npc} hasn't drunk for several years now - not out of remorse, his health just won't allow it. But today, for the first time, he himself spoke of the past: the shouting, the smashed crockery, your tears as a child.
ev.v_rel_father_old.text.4: The old man sits by the hearth turning an empty cup in his hands, a cup he no longer touches. "What a misery I made of your life," says {npc}, without looking up.
ev.v_rel_father_old.text.5: {npc}, your father, sent word through the neighbors: he can no longer make the walk himself. You came, and as soon as he saw you he began to weep and ask forgiveness for everything at once.
ev.v_rel_father_old.text.6: {npc} mixes up days and names, but he remembers those nights clearly - more clearly than you'd like. Today he grabbed your hand and whispered: "Forgive me."
ev.v_rel_father_old.text.7: {npc} has grown frail, and there's no one to look after him. The neighbors say he asks about you every day and wants you to know he regrets every day he drank away.
ev.v_rel_father_old.text.8: {npc} has taken to his bed, and the healer says he won't rise again. Staring at the ceiling, he remembers how you used to hide from him as a child, and asks your forgiveness.
ev.v_rel_father_old.text.9: You dropped in to see your father, and {npc} met you at the door, leaning heavily on a stick. "I've wanted to say it all my life… forgive me for those years."
ev.v_rel_father_old.text.10: {npc} can no longer even hold a spoon - his hands shake after so many years of drink. He brought it up himself: "This is my punishment. Only you forgive me."
ev.v_rel_father_old.text.11: At the feast {npc}, for the first time you can remember, didn't touch a drop. In the evening he drew you aside and, stumbling over the words, asked forgiveness for the years gone by.
ev.v_rel_father_old.text.12: You came back to the house you grew up in - {npc} had sent for you. The same doorstep, the same corner where you used to hide. And he himself, grey and stooped, is asking your forgiveness.
ev.v_rel_father_old.text.13: An old friend of your father's passed on the message: {npc} is failing and wants to see you. He's waiting to ask your forgiveness - and is afraid you won't come.
ev.v_rel_father_old.text.14: {npc} is living out his days in silence: his old drinking companions have scattered, and he is alone. Today he told you: "You're the only one who still comes. Forgive me, if you can."
ev.v_rel_father_old.text.15: For the first time you see {npc} cry. He says that every night he remembers coming home drunk, and he asks for only one thing - your forgiveness.
ev.v_rel_father_old.text.16: {npc} sits all day on the bench outside the house, watching the road. When you came up, he said he'd been waiting a long time for you - to ask your forgiveness.
ev.f_m_saint_day.text.3: For the feast of the patron saint you bought a candle and set it before the holy image. People sang all around, and the flame trembled with everyone's breath.
ev.f_m_saint_day.text.4: On the saint's day a procession went round the district: the holy image in front, and behind it everyone, young and old. You walked in the crowd and gave alms to the beggars at the gate along the way.
ev.f_m_saint_day.text.5: The saint's feast brought the whole district together. After the service a common table was laid in the meadow: everyone brought what they could, and you gave your share without a second thought.
ev.f_m_saint_day.text.6: On the saint's day the line to his relics stretched all the way from the gate. You waited it out to the end, kissed the reliquary and left a modest gift.
ev.f_m_saint_day.text.7: Today is the feast of a saint everyone in the district knows: the church is packed, and sweets are sold at the door. You bought a handful and gave half of it away to the children.
ev.f_m_saint_day.text.8: Pilgrims came from far away for the saint's feast - dusty, weary, eyes shining. You fed one of them and listened until evening to his tales of distant monasteries.
ev.f_m_saint_day.text.9: On the saint's day people bring their promised gifts to the church: linen, honey, wax. You brought yours too - small, but from the heart.
ev.f_m_saint_day.text.10: At the saint's feast musicians played, and even the old folk got up to dance. You spent a little on treats and came home tired and happy.
ev.f_m_saint_day.text.11: They say that on his feast day the saint grants one request. You bought a thin little candle and couldn't decide for a long time what to ask for.
ev.f_m_saint_day.text.12: On the saint's day the water in the church was blessed, and everyone hurried to take some home. You gave the sexton a small offering for a little jug and carried it home like a treasure.
ev.f_m_saint_day.text.13: For the saint's feast the whole street decorated their doors with greenery. You wove a wreath and bought a honey cake from a peddler - a day like this comes once a year.
ev.f_m_saint_day.text.14: On the eve of the saint's day the service went on all night. By dawn you could barely stand, and you left your mite on the plate by the door, but when they sang the final hymn your weariness vanished.
ev.f_m_saint_day.text.15: On the saint's day bread was handed out to the poor at the church, and you too put your share in the common basket. The priest blessed everyone at once, and the crowd fell wonderfully quiet.
ev.f_m_saint_day.text.16: The saint's feast fell on market day, and half the town didn't know where to go first - to the service or the stalls. You managed both and came home with an empty purse and a light heart.
ev.c_river.text.1: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} ran off to the river with the neighbors' children without asking and slipped on the rocks. A fisherman hauled {g=npc_sex:him|her} out by the collar - soaked, terrified and very proud of {g=npc_sex:himself|herself}.
ev.c_river.text.2: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} tagged along after the washerwomen to the river, went after a floating rag and went right under. One of the women hauled {g=npc_sex:him|her} out by the collar - soaked and very pleased with {g=npc_sex:himself|herself}.
ev.c_river.thank.2: Thank the washerwoman and let it go
ev.c_river.thank.ok.2: The washerwoman went off with a basket full of treats. You went on flinching at the word "river" for a long time.
ev.c_river.text.3: {npc} ran off to the crossing without asking to look at the boats and fell off the landing stage into the water. The ferryman hooked {g=npc_sex:him|her} out with an oar like a fish and carried {g=npc_sex:him|her} back to you on his shoulder.
ev.c_river.thank.3: Thank the ferryman and let it go
ev.c_river.thank.ok.3: The ferryman got a bundle of food and chuckled about it for a long time. As for you, you've given the crossing a wide berth ever since.
ev.c_river.text.4: {npc} went swimming with the bigger children and misjudged the depth. A neighbor's lad pulled {g=npc_sex:him|her} out - every bit as frightened as the one who'd been drowning.
ev.c_river.thank.4: Thank the lad and let it go
ev.c_river.thank.ok.4: The lad got a basket of treats and became the hero of the whole street. You went on flinching at the word "river" for a long time.
ev.c_river.text.5: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} ran off to the watering place to look at the herd and tumbled down the steep bank. The herdsman jumped in after {g=npc_sex:him|her} and carried {g=npc_sex:him|her} out - coughing and beaming.
ev.c_river.thank.5: Thank the herdsman and let it go
ev.c_river.thank.ok.5: The herdsman took home a basket of treats and promised to keep an eye on the bank. Your heart still skipped a beat at the sight of water for a long time.
ev.c_river.text.6: {npc} followed the water carrier to the river and, while he was filling his jars, waded in up to the neck. The water carrier dropped his jars and dragged {g=npc_sex:him|her} out onto the bank.
ev.c_river.thank.6: Thank the water carrier and let it go
ev.c_river.thank.ok.6: You paid the water carrier for his broken jar and a little extra besides. You went on flinching at the word "river" for a long time.
ev.c_river.text.7: {npc} was sailing bark boats on the river and chased one right out into the current. A passing wanderer threw himself into the water fully clothed and pulled {g=npc_sex:him|her} out by the collar.
ev.c_river.thank.7: Thank the wanderer and let it go
ev.c_river.thank.ok.7: The wanderer went on his way in dry clothes with a full belly. You kept waking at night at the mere thought of the river for a long time.
ev.c_river.text.8: {npc} ran off to the river without asking to play with the clay and slid down the slippery bank straight into the water. A potter digging clay nearby pulled {g=npc_sex:him|her} out - covered head to toe, like a brand-new pot.
ev.c_river.thank.8: Thank the potter and let it go
ev.c_river.thank.ok.8: The potter got a basket of treats and an order for a dozen bowls. You went on flinching at the word "river" for a long time.
ev.c_river.text.9: {npc} clambered into someone's boat by the bank, rocked it and tumbled overboard. The fishermen mending nets nearby fished {g=npc_sex:him|her} out in no time - soaked and not the least bit sorry.
ev.c_river.thank.9: Thank the fishermen and let it go
ev.c_river.thank.ok.9: The fishermen went off with a basket of treats and a new story to tell. Ever since, whenever you pass the bank, you count the boats.
ev.c_river.text.10: {npc} bet the other children {g=npc_sex:he|she} could wade across the river, and halfway over the current knocked {g=npc_sex:him|her} off {g=npc_sex:his|her} feet. A neighbor's girl, tall and bold, grabbed {g=npc_sex:his|her} hand and pulled {g=npc_sex:him|her} into the shallows.
ev.c_river.thank.10: Thank the girl and let it go
ev.c_river.thank.ok.10: The girl got a string of beads and wore it proudly all summer. You went on flinching at the word "river" for a long time.
ev.c_river.text.11: {npc} slipped off the log the children use to run across the channel and got stuck among the snags. A passing stranger heard the cry and pulled {g=npc_sex:him|her} out - and would have left without giving his name if you hadn't caught up with him.
ev.c_river.thank.11: Thank the stranger and let it go
ev.c_river.thank.ok.11: The stranger refused for a long time but took the treats in the end. You went on flinching at the word "river" for a long time.
ev.c_river.text.12: {npc} went into the river after a dropped toy and was swept away by the current. The neighbor's dog leapt in and dragged {g=npc_sex:him|her} by the shirt onto the shallows.
ev.c_river.thank.12: Thank the dog's owner and let it go
ev.c_river.thank.ok.12: The neighbor got a basket of treats, and the dog the best bone of its life. You went on flinching at the word "river" for a long time.
ev.c_river.text.13: {npc} sneaked off for a swim and got caught in a deep pool. An old woman drawing water held out a stick and hauled {g=npc_sex:him|her} onto the bank, scolding so loudly the whole neighborhood heard.
ev.c_river.thank.13: Thank the old woman and let it go
ev.c_river.thank.ok.13: The old woman took the treats and gave another scolding - this time to you. You went on flinching at the word "river" for a long time.
ev.c_river.text.14: {npc} ran off to watch the boats being loaded on the river and fell off the planks. Two porters fished {g=npc_sex:him|her} out with four hands and returned {g=npc_sex:him|her} to you with a bow and a grin.
ev.c_river.thank.14: Thank the porters and let it go
ev.c_river.thank.ok.14: The porters got a basket of treats and spent the whole evening retelling the story. You went on flinching at the word "river" for a long time.
ev.c_river.text.15: {npc} ran down to the river after the festival crowd and slipped on the wet stones. A keeper of the holy place standing by the water caught {g=npc_sex:him|her} by the hem at the last moment.
ev.c_river.thank.15: Thank the holy man and let it go
ev.c_river.thank.ok.15: You brought a gift to the holy place, and the keeper gave the runaway a long blessing. You went on flinching at the word "river" for a long time.
ev.c_river.text.16: {npc} chased dragonflies down to the marshy bank and sank waist-deep in the mud, with the water still rising. A hunter passing by pulled {g=npc_sex:him|her} out like a turnip.
ev.c_river.thank.16: Thank the hunter and let it go
ev.c_river.thank.ok.16: The hunter took the treats and advised you never to take your eyes off the runaway. You went on flinching at the word "river" for a long time.
ev.f_m_lent.text.3: The first day of the fast: the pots were scoured, and even the smell of cooking changed - lean and herby. You sighed and resigned yourself.
ev.f_m_lent.text.4: The fast goes on week after week: porridge, beans, roots - and porridge again. You've grown thinner, but in church in the evenings you pray as you haven't prayed all year.
ev.f_m_lent.text.5: For the fast you resolved not only to give up rich food but to stop swearing too. Going without the food turned out to be much easier.
ev.f_m_lent.text.6: In the middle of the fast you caught yourself thinking about a rich, fatty stew. You drove the thought away with a prayer - and an hour later it was back.
ev.f_m_lent.text.7: In church they read the long prayers of repentance, and you stand through them from start to finish. Your knees ache and your stomach is empty, but your soul feels unusually clear.
ev.f_m_lent.text.8: During the fast the neighbors grew quieter and kinder: fewer quarrels, more alms. Even you forgave an old grudge - somehow it's harder to stay angry on an empty stomach.
ev.f_m_lent.text.9: By the middle of the fast your strength is running low: work goes slower and sleep is shorter. But when the call comes for the evening service, your feet carry you to church on their own.
ev.f_m_lent.text.10: You kept the fast strictly, as you were taught as a child, and in the fourth week you took to your bed for a couple of days. Then you got up - and carried on, only more gently.
ev.f_m_lent.text.11: You're sick to death of fasting food, and you're inventing your hundredth way to cook the same beans. None of them tastes like meat, but by the hundredth you've almost made your peace with it.
ev.f_m_lent.text.12: This Lent, for the first time, you made a real confession - not out of habit, but from the heart. Hunger and silence did their work.
ev.f_m_lent.text.13: The last week of the fast: everyone is waiting for the feast and counting the days. You're so weak you nod off during the service, but inside there is a quiet, stubborn expectation.
ev.f_m_lent.text.14: Lent is a time for alms, and you gave your share of the meal to a beggar. You were hungrier than ever, but for the first time in a year your conscience is quiet.
ev.f_m_lent.text.15: Spring, the fast, empty storerooms: at this time of year you'd go hungry even without any rules. But hunger is easier to bear with prayer - so the old folk say, and you believe them.
ev.f_m_lent.text.16: During the fast nothing rich is cooked in the house, and even the cat walks around offended. You've made it through half already, and it feels like a small feat of heroism.
ev.c_broken_amphora.text.1: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} broke the finest jar in the house and blamed the cat. The cat sits nearby, radiating contempt.
ev.c_broken_amphora.text.1.E03: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} broke the amphora of your best wine and blamed the cat. The cat sits nearby, radiating contempt.
ev.c_broken_amphora.text.2: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} broke the painted bowl and insists it was the dog. The dog wags its tail and seems ready to take the blame.
ev.c_broken_amphora.laugh.ok.2: The two of you swept up the shards, and the dog got a bone for keeping quiet.
ev.c_broken_amphora.punish.ok.2: An evening with no sweets and a broom in hand. {npc} sulks; the dog lies beside {g=npc_sex:him|her} in sympathy.
ev.c_broken_amphora.truth.failure.2: {npc} stuck to the story until the tears came. The dog remained under suspicion.
ev.c_broken_amphora.text.3: The water jar lies in pieces, and your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} explains: it was the wind. A very strong wind, apparently - right inside the house.
ev.c_broken_amphora.laugh.ok.3: The two of you swept up the shards and agreed to keep the door shut against such a treacherous wind from now on.
ev.c_broken_amphora.punish.ok.3: An evening with no sweets and a broom in hand. {npc} sulks and grumbles at the wind.
ev.c_broken_amphora.truth.failure.3: {npc} stuck to the story until the tears came. The wind was never cleared.
ev.c_broken_amphora.text.4: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} broke the clay lamp and swears it was the neighbor boy, who "just happened to drop by." The boy, however, spent all morning in his own yard, as the whole street can testify.
ev.c_broken_amphora.laugh.ok.4: The two of you swept up the shards and spent the evening by the light of the hearth - cozier, if anything.
ev.c_broken_amphora.punish.ok.4: An evening with no sweets and a broom in hand. {npc} sulks and steers clear of the neighbors' yard.
ev.c_broken_amphora.truth.failure.4: {npc} stuck to the story until the tears came. The neighbor boy still doesn't know what he was accused of.
ev.c_broken_amphora.text.5: {npc} dropped your favorite cup and immediately pointed at the cat. The cat was asleep at the other end of the house at the time and is now washing itself in indignation.
ev.c_broken_amphora.text.6: The honey pot is smashed and honey is spreading across the floor, while {npc}, sticky-handed, explains that it was mice. Big mice, apparently. Strong ones.
ev.c_broken_amphora.laugh.6: Laugh - there was hardly any honey left in it anyway
ev.c_broken_amphora.laugh.ok.6: The two of you scrubbed the floor till evening, licking your fingers. The mice never came for their share.
ev.c_broken_amphora.punish.ok.6: An evening with no sweets - especially galling after the honey. {npc} sulks and scrubs the floor.
ev.c_broken_amphora.truth.failure.6: {npc} stuck to the story until the tears came. The mice were never caught.
ev.c_broken_amphora.text.7: {npc} brought you your best comb - in two halves. "It did it by itself," says {npc}, with a look so honest it's almost embarrassing.
ev.c_broken_amphora.laugh.ok.7: You tucked the halves away as a keepsake, and now {npc} combs your hair with {g=npc_sex:his|her} fingers, very solemnly.
ev.c_broken_amphora.punish.ok.7: An evening with no sweets and a broom in hand. {npc} sulks and mutters that things do sometimes break by themselves.
ev.c_broken_amphora.truth.failure.7: {npc} stuck to the story until the tears came. The comb, it seems, broke all by itself.
ev.c_broken_amphora.text.8: The bowl of grain is smashed and grain is everywhere in the yard, while {npc} points at the rooster: he did it. The rooster is proudly pecking up the evidence.
ev.c_broken_amphora.laugh.ok.8: The two of you gathered the shards, and the rooster pecked up the rest - everyone's happy.
ev.c_broken_amphora.punish.ok.8: An evening with no sweets and a broom in hand. {npc} sulks; the rooster gloats.
ev.c_broken_amphora.truth.failure.8: {npc} stuck to the story until the tears came. The rooster remains the chief suspect.
ev.c_broken_amphora.text.9: The storage jar is broken, and {npc} whispers that it was the spirit who lives under the floor. Saw it with {g=npc_sex:his|her} own eyes, honest.
ev.c_broken_amphora.laugh.ok.9: The two of you swept up the shards and, just in case, left a flatbread under the floor for the spirit.
ev.c_broken_amphora.punish.ok.9: An evening with no sweets and a broom in hand. {npc} sulks and glances warily at the floor.
ev.c_broken_amphora.truth.failure.9: {npc} stuck to the story until the tears came. Ever since, everyone in the house has been a little afraid of the spirit under the floor.
ev.c_broken_amphora.text.10: {npc} broke the festive platter and blamed it all on a friend whom nobody but {g=npc_sex:him|her} has ever seen.
ev.c_broken_amphora.laugh.ok.10: The two of you swept up the shards, and the invisible friend, we're told, is very sorry too.
ev.c_broken_amphora.punish.ok.10: An evening with no sweets and a broom in hand. {npc} sulks: it's unfair to be punished for someone else's crime.
ev.c_broken_amphora.truth.failure.10: {npc} stuck to the story until the tears came. The invisible friend, it seems, never confessed.
ev.c_broken_amphora.text.11: {npc} was kicking a ball around the house and knocked a clay pot off the shelf. Now, with a sorrowful face, {g=npc_sex:he|she} explains that the cat pushed it. The cat, sitting on that very shelf, doesn't argue.
ev.c_broken_amphora.text.12: After the guests left you found the shards of a jug in the corner. {npc} insists it was the guest - though the guest didn't leave his seat all evening.
ev.c_broken_amphora.laugh.ok.12: The two of you swept up the shards and decided the guest needn't hear about it.
ev.c_broken_amphora.punish.ok.12: An evening with no sweets and a broom in hand. {npc} sulks and announces that there will never be guests again.
ev.c_broken_amphora.truth.failure.12: {npc} stuck to the story until the tears came. Luckily, nobody ever asked the guest.
ev.c_broken_amphora.text.13: {npc} broke a jug and, without batting an eye, declared that you'd put it too close to the edge. You have to admit, there's no arguing with that.
ev.c_broken_amphora.laugh.ok.13: The two of you swept up the shards, and you honestly admitted your share of the blame.
ev.c_broken_amphora.punish.ok.13: An evening with no sweets and a broom in hand. {npc} sulks: surely the one who put it there is to blame.
ev.c_broken_amphora.truth.failure.13: {npc} stuck to the story until the tears came. You had to agree that the edge of a table is a dangerous place.
ev.c_broken_amphora.text.14: {npc} broke the bowl of dough and, wiping {g=npc_sex:his|her} hands on {g=npc_sex:his|her} shirt, announced: the cat. There's no dough on the cat's whiskers - but the culprit's face is covered in flour.
ev.c_broken_amphora.text.15: The jug on the windowsill is broken, and {npc} tells a whole tale: a huge bird flew in the window, knocked everything over and flew off. With every retelling the bird gets bigger.
ev.c_broken_amphora.laugh.ok.15: The two of you swept up the shards, and you later enjoyed retelling the bird story to the neighbors.
ev.c_broken_amphora.punish.ok.15: An evening with no sweets and a broom in hand. {npc} sulks and keeps glancing at the window in case the bird comes to the rescue.
ev.c_broken_amphora.truth.failure.15: {npc} stuck to the story until the tears came. Ever since, the huge bird has been expected at every window.
ev.c_broken_amphora.text.16: {npc} broke the expensive vase brought from far away and promptly blamed the cat. The cat pointedly left the house and didn't come back until dinner.
ev.c_broken_amphora.laugh.16: Laugh - you never liked it anyway
ev.d_rumor.text.1: The neighbor women at the well fall silent whenever you come near. At last one of them whispers: {npc} has been calling on {g=npc_sex:a certain young widow|a certain cloth merchant} far too often. Maybe it's only spiteful tongues…
ev.d_rumor.text.2: The market woman, wrapping your purchase, sighs sympathetically: {npc} has been going to the far end of town rather often lately, to see {g=npc_sex:a certain widow who spins yarn|a certain widowed potter}. "It's not me saying it, it's what people say…"
ev.d_rumor.ask.success.2: {npc} blushed and confessed: {g=npc_sex:he'd|she'd} been secretly ordering a festival present for you. The surprise is ruined, but your heart is light.
ev.d_rumor.follow.success.2: You crept along behind for half a day and saw {npc} haggling over some new thing - for you, as it turned out that evening. Embarrassing - but your heart is light.
ev.d_rumor.text.3: {npc} comes home after dark more and more often, and a neighbor has twice "happened" to mention seeing {g=npc_sex:him by the house of a certain young widow|her by the shop of a certain handsome trader}.
ev.d_rumor.ask.success.3: {npc} sighed wearily: {g=npc_sex:he's|she's} been taking extra work in the evenings to pay off an old debt and was ashamed to tell you. You promised to help - and you no longer listen to the neighbors.
ev.d_rumor.follow.success.3: You followed until evening and saw {npc} hauling other people's sacks for pay - to settle an old debt. Embarrassing - but your heart is light.
ev.d_rumor.text.4: You found a stranger's scarf among your things, and a day later a neighbor whispered that {npc} often calls on {g=npc_sex:a certain young widow|a certain visiting merchant}.
ev.d_rumor.ask.success.4: {npc} laughed: the scarf was given at a shop to wrap a purchase in, and {g=npc_sex:he|she} delivers orders to that house. You no longer believe the gossip.
ev.d_rumor.follow.success.4: You spent half a day hiding round a corner and saw nothing but {npc} hand over an order and leave without lingering a moment. Embarrassing - but your heart is light.
ev.d_rumor.text.5: At the festival {npc} spent the whole evening laughing with {g=npc_sex:a certain young widow|a certain visiting trader}, and now the whole street is talking about it. They say the two have met since.
ev.d_rumor.ask.success.5: {npc} was surprised: {g=npc_sex:the widow is an old acquaintance|the trader is an old acquaintance} from back home, and they talked of nothing but old times. At last you could breathe again.
ev.d_rumor.follow.success.5: You tracked down their meeting and saw {npc} handing over a bundle for mutual friends back home. Embarrassing - but your heart is light.
ev.d_rumor.text.6: A neighbor winked at you with a smirk: {npc}, he hinted, has found some comfort with {g=npc_sex:a certain widow|a certain trader} across town. You brushed it off, but the words stuck like a splinter.
ev.d_rumor.ask.success.6: {npc} went purple with rage - not at you, but at the neighbor: he's owed you money for ages and is getting back at you for the reminders. Your heart eased at once.
ev.d_rumor.follow.success.6: You followed for half a day and saw nothing but {npc} doing the rounds of debtors and squabbling over money owed. Embarrassing - but your heart is light.
ev.d_rumor.text.7: {npc} bought some expensive cloth and hid it, and the neighbor women whisper that {g=npc_sex:he was seen calling on a certain young widow|she was seen calling on a certain unmarried trader}.
ev.d_rumor.ask.success.7: {npc} threw up {g=npc_sex:his|her} hands: the cloth is for you, for the festival, and {g=npc_sex:he|she} went to that house to have it sewn. So much for the surprise - but your heart is at peace.
ev.d_rumor.follow.success.7: You followed and saw {npc} handing the cloth over to be sewn and explaining at length how to take the measurements. A month later the new garment was yours. Embarrassing - but your heart is light.
ev.d_rumor.text.8: They say {npc} goes to pray every day - and every time {g=npc_sex:a certain young widow|a certain widowed trader} turns up there too. Too much of a coincidence, they whisper at the well.
ev.d_rumor.ask.success.8: {npc} looked down: {g=npc_sex:he's|she's} been praying for your health - you were ill for so long. The {g=npc_sex:widow|widower} is simply praying for {g=npc_sex:her|his} own.
ev.d_rumor.follow.success.8: You stood in the shadows for half a day and saw nothing but {npc} praying, looking at no one. Embarrassing - but your heart is light.
ev.d_rumor.text.9: An old gossip who has never spared anyone announced loudly in front of everyone that {npc} visits {g=npc_sex:a certain widowed healer|a certain visiting physician} far too often.
ev.d_rumor.ask.success.9: {npc} was embarrassed: {g=npc_sex:he'd|she'd} been going for treatment for some trifling ailment and didn't want to worry you. The ailment passed, and so did the suspicion.
ev.d_rumor.follow.success.9: You hid round a corner for half a day and saw {npc} come out with a little pot of ointment, wincing. Embarrassing - but your heart is light.
ev.d_rumor.text.10: Now grain, now yarn goes missing from the house, and a neighbor whispers that {npc} carries them to {g=npc_sex:a certain poor widow|a certain poor widower} on the edge of town. Pity, or something worse - who can tell?
ev.d_rumor.ask.success.10: {npc} admitted it: the {g=npc_sex:widow|widower} was left with small children and not a crust of bread, and walking past was impossible. You were silent a long time, then packed another bundle.
ev.d_rumor.follow.success.10: You followed and saw {npc} leave a bundle on the doorstep and walk away without even knocking. Embarrassing - but your heart is light.
ev.d_rumor.text.11: You woke in the night and {npc} wasn't beside you. In the morning a neighbor, avoiding your eyes, said she'd seen {g=npc_sex:him at the house of a certain widow|her at the house of a certain widower}.
ev.d_rumor.ask.success.11: {npc} laughed: there'd been a call for help in the night - the {g=npc_sex:widow's|widower's} roof had caved in and there was no one else nearby. You no longer believe the gossip.
ev.d_rumor.follow.success.11: For three nights you lay awake keeping watch, and {npc} went nowhere and snored peacefully beside you. Embarrassing - but your heart is light.
ev.d_rumor.text.12: Lately {npc} has been cheerful, humming, taking care with appearances. And at the well they whisper that the reason is {g=npc_sex:a certain young widow|a certain young trader} from the next street.
ev.d_rumor.ask.success.12: {npc} was offended at first, then burst out laughing: business has finally picked up, that's all. You felt foolish - and happy.
ev.d_rumor.follow.success.12: You followed for half a day and saw nothing but {npc} humming at work and looking at no one. Embarrassing - but your heart is light.
ev.d_rumor.text.13: While you were out, {g=npc_sex:a certain young widow|a certain cloth merchant} came to the house, the neighbors whisper. And for some reason {npc} never mentioned it.
ev.d_rumor.title.13: A Visitor While You Were Out
ev.d_rumor.ask.success.13: {npc} shrugged: it was about an old debt, and {g=npc_sex:he|she} didn't mention it so as not to spoil your evening. You no longer believe the gossip.
ev.d_rumor.follow.success.13: For several days you watched the house and saw {npc} pay the visitor back right on the doorstep, without even inviting them in. Embarrassing - but your heart is light.
ev.d_rumor.text.14: When you went down to the river, the women on the landing fell silent, and then one of them said: {npc} helps {g=npc_sex:a certain widow|a certain widower} with the chores far too often.
ev.d_rumor.ask.success.14: {npc} shrugged: the {g=npc_sex:widow|widower} is a childhood friend with no one else to help. "Come with me tomorrow," {npc} suggested.
ev.d_rumor.follow.success.14: You followed and saw {npc} mending the fence of a tumbledown hut - and the {g=npc_sex:widow is a frail old woman|widower is a frail old man}. Embarrassing - but your heart is light.
ev.d_rumor.text.15: {npc} has started hiding savings, and someone saw {g=npc_sex:him passing something to a certain young widow|her passing something to a certain trader} at the gate.
ev.d_rumor.ask.success.15: {npc} sighed and told you everything: {g=npc_sex:he'd|she'd} been saving up for a present for you, and the {g=npc_sex:widow|trader} had only agreed to get hold of it. You no longer believe the gossip.
ev.d_rumor.follow.success.15: You followed and saw {npc} paying a deposit on a piece of jewelry and taking ages to choose which would suit you best. Embarrassing - but your heart is light.
ev.d_rumor.text.16: At a neighbor's wedding someone sang a mocking song about {g=npc_sex:a husband who kept visiting a widow|a wife who kept visiting a merchant} - and for some reason everyone looked at you. And {npc} sat there red as a beet.
ev.d_rumor.ask.success.16: {npc} laughed: the song was made up about someone else, and the blush was from the stuffy room and embarrassment on that poor soul's behalf. You no longer believe the gossip.
ev.d_rumor.follow.success.16: For several days you followed and made sure: {npc} goes nowhere but to work and home. Embarrassing - but your heart is light.
ev.c_teacher.text.1: The teacher complains that your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} counts flies instead of letters and has had the rod twice already. {npc} insists the teacher is simply mean.
ev.c_teacher.text.2: The teacher has come to complain: instead of doing exercises {npc} draws birds, fish and the teacher himself in the margins - with a very long nose. {npc} thinks it's a good likeness and there's nothing to punish.
ev.c_teacher.text.3: The teacher complains that your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} falls asleep right in the middle of lessons and, when woken, says the teacher drones like a beetle in a jar.
ev.c_teacher.text.4: It turns out {npc} hasn't made it to the teacher for a week: {g=npc_sex:he|she} turns off to the river on the way. The teacher threatens expulsion, and {npc} says the teacher beats you for nothing anyway.
ev.c_teacher.text.5: The teacher reports that {npc} got into a fight with another pupil right in the middle of a lesson. {npc} swears {g=npc_sex:he|she} didn't start it, yet {g=npc_sex:he|she} was the only one punished.
ev.c_teacher.text.6: The teacher is outraged: {npc} corrected him in front of everyone - and, worst of all, was right. Now the teacher finds fault with every stroke, and {npc} goes to lessons as if to an execution.
ev.c_teacher.text.7: {npc} came home with swollen palms: the teacher beat {g=npc_sex:him|her} with a stick over a botched lesson. The teacher says it was for laziness; {npc} says {g=npc_sex:he|she} simply didn't understand the explanation.
ev.c_teacher.text.8: The teacher complains that {npc} copies from the pupil on the next bench and knows nothing on {g=npc_sex:his|her} own. {npc} is indignant: the teacher explains things so fast nobody could keep up.
ev.c_teacher.text.9: {npc} mimics the teacher so well that all the pupils are rolling with laughter. The teacher came to you white with fury, and {npc} insists the teacher simply has no sense of humor.
ev.c_teacher.text.10: Every morning {npc} cries and doesn't want to go to the teacher. And the teacher says the child is lazy and strictness will do {g=npc_sex:him|her} nothing but good.
ev.c_teacher.text.11: The teacher complains that {npc} is quick with sums but refuses to learn to write. "I don't need it, I'm going to be a trader," {npc} announces, and the teacher reaches for the rod again.
ev.c_teacher.text.12: The teacher says {npc} stares out the window all lesson and gives answers that make no sense. {npc} insists it's more interesting outside, and the teacher is mean and boring.
ev.c_teacher.text.13: {npc} knocked ink over the teacher's scroll, and the teacher still hasn't recovered. As punishment {npc} had to copy the same line a hundred times and swears never to go back.
ev.c_teacher.text.14: The teacher complains that {npc} stubbornly says nothing in lessons - not a word, even under the rod. At home {npc} explains: "He'll say it's wrong anyway."
ev.c_teacher.text.15: {npc} is late to the teacher every day and gets rapped on the knuckles for it. The teacher demands strictness, and {npc} complains that the teacher picks on {g=npc_sex:him|her} alone.
ev.c_teacher.text.16: At an examination in front of distinguished guests {npc} couldn't read a single line, and the teacher came to you full of reproaches. {npc} whispers that fear of the teacher makes all the characters scatter.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.1: A draft wakes you: there's a gaping hole in the storeroom wall, and the chest with your savings for a rainy day is gone. Hurried footsteps still echo down the street. Years of saving are in someone else's hands.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.1.athens: A draft wakes you: “wall-diggers” have tunneled through the mud-brick wall of your storeroom, and the chest with your savings for a rainy day is gone. Hurried footsteps still echo down the street. Years of saving are in someone else's hands.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.2: A splintering crash wakes you: the storeroom door has been forced, and the chest with your savings for a rainy day is gone. Two shadows flit across the yard and dart for the gate. Years of saving are in someone else's hands.
ev.t_night_burglary.accept.ok.2: You put in a new door with a stout bolt and decided: from now on your money stays with people you can trust. An expensive lesson, but you'll never forget it.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.3: In the night dust sifted down from the ceiling: thieves had pulled apart the roof over the storeroom and let themselves down on a rope. By the time you ran in, the chest was gone, and footsteps were fading away over the neighbors' roofs.
ev.t_night_burglary.accept.ok.3: You had the roof redone and decided: from now on your money stays with people you can trust, not under your own roof. An expensive lesson, but you'll never forget it.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.4: You woke in the night because of the silence: the dog that barks at every shadow lies drugged, and the chest of savings has vanished from the storeroom. Beyond the fence someone's footsteps are still crunching away.
ev.t_night_burglary.accept.ok.4: You got a second dog and decided: from now on your money stays with people you can trust. An expensive lesson, but you'll never forget it.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.5: While the whole street was out celebrating, someone climbed into your house through a window. You came home after midnight: shutters flung open, the money chest gone, and running footsteps still echoing in the alley.
ev.t_night_burglary.accept.ok.5: You boarded up the window and decided: from now on someone always stays home on feast days, and your money stays with people you can trust. An expensive lesson, but you'll never forget it.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.6: A storm raged in the night, and over the thunder you didn't hear the thieves breaking through the storeroom wall. Only a banging door woke you: the money chest is gone, and footsteps are splashing away through the puddles.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.7: In the middle of the night you heard a rustling in the yard: a ladder against the wall, the upper window flung open, and strangers' hands already heaving the chest of your savings over the fence.
ev.t_night_burglary.accept.ok.7: You raised the fence higher and decided: from now on your money stays with people you can trust, not at home. An expensive lesson, but you'll never forget it.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.8: A dull thud woke you in the night. The storeroom lock has been knocked off, and the chest with the money you'd put by for old age is gone. Hurried footsteps are fading in the street.
ev.t_night_burglary.accept.ok.8: You hung a new lock, though you know it won't stop thieves, and gave your money to people you can trust for safekeeping. An expensive lesson, but you'll never forget it.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.9: You opened your eyes and in the glow of the embers saw a stranger's shadow: it snatched up the money chest and slipped out the door. You leapt up - there's only the echo of footsteps in the street.
ev.t_night_burglary.accept.ok.9: You started barring the door at night with two bolts and decided: from now on your money stays with people you can trust. An expensive lesson, but you'll never forget it.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.10: You came home from the fair with your takings and put them in the chest with your old savings. And that night someone broke through the storeroom wall - they must have followed you from the market. The chest is gone; footsteps are pounding away in the distance.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.11: In the night a shed went up in flames on the next street, and everyone ran to put it out - you too. When you got back, there was a gaping hole in the storeroom wall and the chest of savings was gone. Somewhere in the dark, running feet can still be heard.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.12: Thieves climbed the fence from the waste ground, wrenched off the shutters and carried out the money chest. You woke to a shutter banging in the wind - the footsteps of the fleeing thieves can still be heard beyond the fence.
ev.t_night_burglary.accept.ok.12: You put up new shutters, built the fence higher and decided: from now on your money stays with people you can trust. An expensive lesson, but you'll never forget it.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.13: Toward dawn the storeroom floor caved in: thieves had dug a tunnel from the waste ground and pulled the chest out from below. You ran in at the noise - nothing in the pit but clods of earth, and footsteps fading outside.
ev.t_night_burglary.accept.ok.13: You filled the pit with stones and decided: from now on your money stays with people you can trust, not under the floor. An expensive lesson, but you'll never forget it.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.14: The watchman you paid to guard the place slipped off somewhere tonight. A crash woke you: the gate is open, the money chest is gone, and footsteps are pounding away down the street.
ev.t_night_burglary.accept.ok.14: You sent the watchman packing, put on new bolts and decided: from now on your money stays with people you can trust. An expensive lesson, but you'll never forget it.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.15: On a moonlit night you couldn't sleep and went out into the yard - just in time to see two figures dragging your money chest through a hole in the wall. When they saw you, they ran.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.16: In the middle of the night a neighbor screamed: "Thieves!" You leapt out of bed - there's a hole in the storeroom wall, the money chest is gone, and fleeing shadows are flickering at the end of the street.
